title: Sponsor a work visa
summary: Keep the hire you can’t legally employ yet: pick the visa route with immigration counsel, build the evidence binder, make the labor-market filing the route requires, sign and file the sponsorship petition with the immigration authority, and wait out adjudication. In the US that is the H-1B/O-1/TN strategy call, the LCA with the DOL, and the I-129 petition with USCIS.

parts.title: Pick the visa strategy with immigration counsel
parts.guidance: Give immigration counsel the role, work locations, employing entity, qualifications, immigration history and desired start date. Compare feasible classifications and their evidence, timing, filing and cost implications, including current policy changes. Agree the strategy before collecting route-specific documents. Establish which of the filing steps below apply to the chosen route and identify any separate consular or admission work needed for the person to start.

geoResolutions.label: The classification call is between H-1B (lottery-gated specialty occupation), O-1, TN and the other I-129 classes
The route is a Home Office sponsor licence plus Certificates of Sponsorship for Skilled Worker visas — salary-threshold based, no lottery
Non-EU hiring runs on the EU Blue Card and Skilled Immigration Act routes — salary-threshold based, no lottery
geoResolutions.actionLabel: Make it in Germany (EU Blue Card)

geoResolutions.label: The startup route is the 'talent' residence card (French Tech Visa) for employees of state-recognised innovative companies, on a salary threshold of about twice the SMIC
geoResolutions.actionLabel: French Tech Visa for Employees (talent card)

geoResolutions.label: AIMA issues residence visas and permits for highly qualified activity plus the EU Blue Card — salary-threshold based, no lottery
The startup rail is the Global Talent Stream: an employer-driven LMIA category for tech occupations with a two-week processing standard
Foreign hires come in on an Employment Visa from Indian missions (salary floor around US$25,000, role not routinely fillable locally); there is no sponsor-licence system

parts.title: Assemble the evidence binder (degrees, press, comp data)
parts.guidance: Organize the evidence around counsel’s checklist for the chosen classification. Collect the requested employer, role and candidate documents, identifying translations, evaluations or explanations still needed. Reconcile names, dates and employment facts across the packet, and distinguish supporting evidence from unverified claims. Give counsel an indexed binder and the specific gaps so the petition can be prepared from accurate facts.

parts.title: Make the labor-market filing the route requires
parts.guidance: If the selected route requires a labor-market attestation or test, reconcile the job, wage, worksites and employment period with counsel. The employer’s authorized representative must understand and approve the required attestations before submission. Address the related notice and employer obligations identified for the case, then track the application in the authorized channel. Send the certified document or correction request to counsel for the next filing decision.

references.title: DOL: H-1B, H-1B1 and E-3 professional workers

verify.how: The LCA returns status Certified in the FLAG portal (ETA-9035) — required before the petition can be filed.

geoResolutions.label: File the LCA (ETA-9035) with the Department of Labor in the FLAG portal; certification is required before the I-129 can be filed
The Global Talent Stream filing is an employer-driven LMIA with a labour-market benefits plan commitment

parts.title: Wait for the labor-market certification
parts.guidance: Check the submitted case through the employer’s or counsel’s authorized account. Send returned applications or factual discrepancies to counsel before resubmission. When certified, compare the document with the proposed petition and update the hiring plan from the actual result. A planning estimate or elapsed time does not establish certification or permission to work.

references.title: DOL: H-1B, H-1B1 and E-3 professional workers

geoResolutions.label: The LCA certifies in about 7 business days; track the ETA-9035 status in FLAG
The Global Talent Stream carries a two-week processing standard

parts.title: Sign the sponsorship petition
parts.guidance: Present the completed petition and employer declarations to the authorized company signatory with counsel’s explanation of the attestations. Resolve differences in the person, role, worksite, classification or requested dates before signing. The signatory reviews and signs the actual filing version. Return the signed package to counsel with any outstanding filing conditions clearly identified.

geoResolutions.label: The signature goes on Form I-129 and the employer declarations

parts.title: File the petition with the immigration authority
parts.guidance: Have counsel check the filing route, form edition, evidence, applicable fees and processing request for the selected classification. Obtain the employer’s authorization for that package and payment, then submit through the confirmed channel. Check delivery or receipt status and resolve a rejection before resubmitting. Give the hiring owner the actual case status and any effect on the start plan.

verify.how: USCIS issues a Form I-797C receipt notice with a case number, and the case appears in USCIS case status.

cost.note: The I-129 filing fee varies by classification and petitioner size, with additional mandatory fees (fraud prevention, ACWIA, asylum program) — see the published USCIS fee schedule.

geoResolutions.label: File the I-129 with USCIS; the I-797C receipt notice carries the case number
Issue the Certificate of Sponsorship under the sponsor licence; the candidate applies on it for the Skilled Worker visa
The talent-card attestation request runs on the official démarches portal
geoResolutions.actionLabel: French Tech Visa for Employees (talent card)

geoResolutions.label: The residence visa or permit application runs through AIMA
The Employment Visa application goes to the Indian mission; there is no employer petition to file
The work-permit application follows the certified LMIA

parts.title: Immigration-authority adjudication
parts.guidance: Track agency notices and response dates from the actual case correspondence. Gather requested facts for counsel and obtain the employer’s approval for a substantive response or strategy change. When a decision arrives, ask counsel what it permits, its validity and any consular, admission or status steps still required. Update the candidate’s start plan from that interpretation, including steps still required after petition approval.

geoResolutions.label: USCIS adjudicates the petition; track notices and RFEs in the case status, and plan any consular or admission steps after approval

parts.title: Update payroll and right-to-work records on approval
parts.guidance: Have counsel and the people lead confirm when the person may work for this employer from the applicable approval, status and admission documents. The authorized representative completes the verification or reverification the jurisdiction requires while respecting employee document choice. Payroll records the cleared start or status change. Keep immigration and identity documents restricted, and assign any future reverification identified by the review.

references.title: USCIS: Completing Supplement B, Reverification and Rehires

geoResolutions.label: The authorized I-9 representative completes Section 2 verification or the Supplement B reverification
Long-stay Employment Visa holders register with the FRRO after arrival

metadata.supportReason: Immigration counsel drives strategy and the filings; the agent assembles the evidence binder and tracks the case. The government portals, the signed petition, and the adjudication wait are irreducibly manual.

geoNotes.summary: Foreign hires come in on an Employment Visa issued by Indian missions — salary floor around US$25,000, role must not be routinely fillable locally — with post-arrival FRRO registration for long stays; there is no sponsor-licence system.
The company first gets a sponsor licence from the Home Office, then issues Certificates of Sponsorship for Skilled Worker visas — salary-threshold based, with no H-1B-style annual lottery.
Hiring non-EU talent runs on the EU Blue Card and Skilled Immigration Act routes — salary-threshold based, no lottery, with the government's Make it in Germany portal as the canonical guide.
geoNotes.actionLabel: Make it in Germany (EU Blue Card)

geoNotes.summary: The startup route is the 'talent' residence card: employees of state-recognised innovative companies (French Tech Visa) get a multi-year permit on a salary threshold of about twice the SMIC — no lottery; the attestation request runs on the official démarches portal.
geoNotes.actionLabel: French Tech Visa for Employees (talent card)

geoNotes.summary: Hiring non-EU talent runs through AIMA (which absorbed SEF in 2023): residence visas and permits for highly qualified activity plus the EU Blue Card — salary-threshold based, with no lottery.

The startup rail is the Global Talent Stream: an employer-driven LMIA category for tech occupations with a two-week processing standard for the work permit — no lottery, but a labour-market benefits plan commitment.
Foreign hires run on sojourn statuses (typically E-7 for specialty workers, D-8 for investor-executives of a foreign-invested company), applied for and extended through HiKorea.
